preset.text: 4 players in 2 teams (Red & Blue) — partners sit across from each other. The deck has only 24 cards: 9, 10, J, Q, K, A of each suit. Each hand is 5 tricks. First team to 10 points wins!

When a suit is NOT trump, cards rank low → high:
9 → 10 → J → Q → K → A (highest).
So in any non-trump suit, the Ace is king.

Each hand, one suit becomes trump — trump beats every non-trump card.

Inside the trump suit, the Jacks get special names:
• Right Bower = Jack of trump → highest card in the whole deck
• Left Bower = Jack of the same-color suit → second highest, and it counts as trump too!

Full ranking when Hearts is trump, highest → lowest:
J♥ (Right Bower) > J♦ (Left Bower) > A♥ > K♥ > Q♥ > 10♥ > 9♥

Why is J♦ in there? Hearts and Diamonds are both red, so the J of the same-color suit joins the trump suit for this hand.
Same-color pairs: ♥ ↔ ♦ and ♠ ↔ ♣.

Each hand starts with the top card of the kitty flipped face-up. Starting left of the dealer, going clockwise, each player chooses:
• Pass
• Order it up — accept the flipped card's suit as trump

If anyone orders up, the dealer picks up the flipped card and discards one. The ordering team becomes the makers and must win at least 3 tricks.

If all 4 players pass, the flipped card is turned down and a second round begins. Each player can:
• Pass
• Name any other suit as trump (you can't pick the rejected suit)

Whoever names trump becomes a maker and needs 3+ tricks. If all 4 pass again, the hand is thrown in and re-dealt.

Scoring per hand:
• Makers win 3–4 tricks → 1 point
• Makers win all 5 (a march) → 2 points
• Makers win fewer than 3 (euchred!) → opponents get 2 points

Playing: you must follow the lead suit when you can. Heads-up: the Left Bower counts as trump, NOT its printed suit — so if Hearts is trump and someone leads Diamonds, your J♦ is not a Diamond. The app enforces legal plays automatically.
